title: These Midterm Races Will Decide Data Centers' Political Fate
source_used: WIRED (Power Play column by Molly Taft)
key_facts: Opposition to data centres is bipartisan, with many Republicans breaking from President Trump; at least five candidates have been given a derogatory 'Data Center [Name]' nickname by opponents.
The National Republican Senatorial Committee warned in August that Democrat Sherrod Brown was hitting Senator Jon Husted so hard on data centres in the Ohio Senate race that it could tip the result.
Senate Democrats torpedoed a Husted-sponsored bill modelled on the White House ratepayer protection pledge; Chuck Schumer called it toothless.
At least 20 candidates in the 36 governor races have promised some kind of data centre moratorium if elected, per research from Multistate.
The only true hyperscale moratorium in the US was signed in July by New York Governor Kathy Hochul.
Texas Governor Greg Abbott has gone from welcoming data centres to a de facto moratorium on permits in under a year; his opponent Gina Hinojosa says he has not gone far enough.
Voters in eight states face more than 30 local ballot measures on data centres; Ohio accounts for more than half. The election is 3 Nov 2026.
quote_evidence: At least 20 candidates in the 36 gubernatorial races have promised to enact some kind of data center moratorium if elected, according to research from Multistate.
Voters in eight states are looking at more than 30 local ballot measures around data centers.
why_it_matters_hint: Data centres have become a campaign issue that could affect tight races and where large data centres can be built.
notes: Weekly opinion-and-reporting column; the judgement that the issue could swing races is the columnist's. Subject is politics of data centres; kept ENE per the chunk default (it could also sit under POL).
